interface.signature: def findHeight(N: int, arr: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.description: N is the number of nodes in the binary tree, constrained between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(arr) == N and all(0 <= x <= 10**5 for x in arr)
preconditions.description: arr is a list of length N where each element is a parent index (0 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10^5).
Exactly one element in arr is -1, representing the root node.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < N for i in range(N))
preconditions.description: Node indices are valid (0 to N-1).

postconditions.expression: return_value == max(0, max((-1 if arr[i] == -1 else 1 + findHeight(N, arr)) for i in range(N) if (lambda x: x == -1 or (lambda y: y != -1 and (lambda z: z >= 0 and z < N))(arr[x]))(arr[i])) if (lambda x: x == -1 or (lambda y: y != -1 and (lambda z: z >= 0 and z < N))(arr[x]))(arr[i]))
postconditions.description: The function returns the height of the binary tree, defined as the maximum depth from the root to any leaf node. The height is computed recursively by traversing parent-child relationships, where the root has height 0, its children height 1, and so on. The expression ensures correctness by validating parent-child relationships and computing the maximum path length.
